clue.text: What about street in foreign capital providing special accommodation?

indicators.note: in signals that the pieces before it sit inside the foreign city's name

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy, a foreign capital to a British setter

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the exclamation encloses the road abbreviation

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation meaning what?

explanation.surface: A query about which street in some overseas capital offers a particular kind of lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' is the exclamation eh?; 'about' wraps it round the street, and 'in' puts the result within the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A care home for the elderly or convalescent is a special form of residential accommodation.

clue.text: About to have something like macaroni? Not a meal!

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: not here means the A that follows is left out

parts.note: pasta is the class of foods that includes macaroni

explanation.surface: An exclamation that macaroni is not a proper meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a meal!' looks like a denial, but 'Not a' removes the A from PASTA and 'meal' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a meal, a formal word for food taken at one sitting.

clue.text: One of 4 offering protection

definitions.meaning: William ... was Master of the King's Music, one of the royal music masters
something that offers protection, a guard or defence

explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says the 4 (MUSIC MASTERS) were royal: William Shield held the post from 1817.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective guard or screen is a defence, and William Shield was Master of the King's Music.

clue.text: One may be working near horses wanting nothing to drop off

indicators.note: may be working signals the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A stable worker who might be busy near the horses with nothing falling off.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of NEAR HORSES, once the O ('nothing') has dropped off ('wanting ... to drop off'), are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: One who harnesses is a person who puts tack on horses, the one in the clue.

clue.text: Noted schoolteachers?

parts.note: noted suggests famous, but read literally it means teachers of musical notes

explanation.definitionFit: Teachers of music in a school deal in notes, so they are noted teachers in the literal sense.

clue.text: In geographical circle what's discussed includes river

indicators.note: includes means the subject word holds the river's letter within it

parts.note: a topic is the subject under discussion
R is the usual abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Something said about a river that lies within a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude drawn round the globe, circles of geography.

clue.text: Ways Cecil articulated

indicators.note: articulated means spoken aloud, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the British imperialist who founded Rhodesia

explanation.surface: The ways in which Cecil spoke clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads are routes or ways from one place to another.

clue.text: Cloakroom fixture securing one black foreign gown

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the hook encloses the numeral

parts.note: a peg is a hook in a cloakroom for hanging coats
I is the Roman numeral for one
noir is French for black

explanation.surface: A cloakroom peg holding one black dress from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' does double duty in sense only: the gown is French, as is NOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a loose woman's dressing gown, a French word for a garment.

clue.text: Spanish explorer stopping short — check inside vessel

indicators.note: inside means the check word goes into the explorer's shortened name
stopping short means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Hernán Cortés was the Spanish conquistador of Mexico
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: A Spanish explorer halts so his ship can be inspected inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Cortés conquered Mexico; 'stopping short' drops his final S, and 'inside' signals the vet's check going into his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A corvette is a small fast warship, a type of naval vessel.

clue.text: Nun curtailed disturbance in crowd

indicators.note: in places the shortened unrest word inside the throng word

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd of people

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail, the final letter, is cut off

parts.note: a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A nun's account of a cut-short disturbance among a mass of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' clips the last letter of the disturbance, giving a Brazilian city's name, which 'in' sets within the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a priory of nuns is a female religious superior, so a senior nun.

clue.text: One of 4 I learn about

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark from someone saying they are studying something.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says the 4 (MUSIC MASTERS) were royal: Nicholas Lanier was the first Master of the King's Music, under Charles I. 'about' rearranges I LEARN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicholas Lanier was appointed the first Master of the King's Music in 1626, one of the royal composers.

clue.text: Navy may be involved in this plan

definitions.text: Navy may be involved in this plan

parts.words: Navy may be involved in this plan
parts.note: the navy sounds like the fleet, but navy blue is a shade that could feature in a decorating plan

explanation.definitionFit: A colour scheme is a planned arrangement of shades, one of which might be dark blue.

clue.text: Greeting anything that brings soothing

definitions.meaning: the Latin word of welcome, hail!, used as a greeting
an ointment or remedy that calms or soothes

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin salutation means hail, and the noun is a healing ointment that soothes the skin.

clue.text: Enamelware endlessly looked at containing various oils

indicators.note: containing means the studied word holds the reshuffled letters
endlessly means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: to con a text is to study or look at it closely

indicators.note: various signals that the letters of the oil word are mixed up

explanation.surface: Ornamental enamel being studied, with various oils involved.
explanation.walkthrough: To con is an old word for studying; 'endlessly' drops its D, 'various' mixes the oils, and 'containing' wraps one round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is decorative enamel work in which colours are separated by thin metal strips.

clue.text: So to slip cage is a possibility for him?

definitions.text: So to slip cage is a possibility for him?

indicators.note: is a possibility hints that a different arrangement of these letters is possible

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a certain performer might be the one to get out of a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: an escape artist is the person for whom slipping out of a cage is a real possibility.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape artist is a performer who frees himself from locks, chains and cages.

clue.text: Where you might see aileron move? That can be frightening

definitions.text: Where you might see aileron move?
definitions.meaning: an aileron is a hinged flap on an aircraft's wing, so it is seen on top of one
intimidating, making someone feel awed or scared

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as OVER A WING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overawing subdues people with awe or fear, so it can be frightening.

clue.text: Get off eating cold scrap that the butcher may supply

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the dispatch word encloses the other letters

parts.note: to send is to get something off, dispatch it
C stands for cold, as on taps
a rag is a scrap of cloth

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a cold scrap that might come from the butcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrag end is the cheap bony neck of mutton, a cut sold by butchers.

clue.text: German vessel sunk by block of ice almost

indicators.note: in a down clue, sunk by puts the ship below the ice letters
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a berg is an iceberg, a floating block of ice
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: A German ship sunk by an iceberg, recalling the Titanic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts BERG to BER, and in this down clue 'sunk by' sets LINER under it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Berliner is a native of Berlin, so a German person.

clue.text: Unmistakable narratives may be seen in large American churches?

definitions.text: may be seen in large American churches?

parts.note: clear means obvious or unmistakable
stories are narratives

explanation.surface: Plain tales being found inside big churches in the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: A clerestory is the upper row of windows in a large church's nave; CLEARSTORY is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The windowed upper storeys of a church nave are found in big churches, here in the US spelling.

clue.text: One of 4 loveless relations

indicators.note: loveless means the O, love as a score of zero, is removed

parts.note: cousins are relations

explanation.surface: Family members who have no love for one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says the 4 (MUSIC MASTERS) were royal: Sir William Cusins was Master of the Queen's Music under Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: William Cusins served as Master of the Queen's Music from 1870, one of the royal post holders.

clue.text: This person being embraced by cleric brings disgrace

indicators.note: being embraced by means held inside the churchman's title

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman
this person is the setter, me

explanation.surface: The setter, hugged by a churchman, is brought into disrepute.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to lower their dignity, to degrade or shame them.

clue.text: Like some fiction I start to read in French — no good

indicators.note: in places the self word and the reading letter inside the French word
no good means the G for good is removed

parts.note: Gallic means French
ego is Latin for I, the self

indicators.note: start to means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A remark from someone beginning to read in French and finding it no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no good' removes the G for good from the French adjective; 'in' sets the Latin I and the reading letter within what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegorical story is one kind of fiction, in which characters and events stand for hidden meanings.

clue.text: One of 4 given secure university

parts.note: to grab is to seize or secure

explanation.surface: Someone given a place to secure at university.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says the 4 (MUSIC MASTERS) were royal: Louis Grabu was Master of the King's Music under Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Grabu, a French composer, was Master of the King's Music for Charles II.

clue.text: Shrewd troublemaker skirting copper

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the goddess encloses the metal

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin, a troublemaker
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A clever mischief-maker who manages to avoid the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with an acute mind is sharp and perceptive, quick-witted in judgement.

clue.text: Group of nine men, one mad — not a leader among them

indicators.note: not a leader among them means each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Nine men in a group, one of whom has lost his mind, with nobody in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: MEN, ONE and MAD each lose their first letters (M, O, M) to give EN, NE and AD.
explanation.definitionFit: An ennead is a set of nine, from the Greek word for nine, as in Plotinus's Enneads.

clue.text: Information's the thing I have in case

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
it stands for the thing
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Some information, holding the item I have in a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammatical case, not a suitcase.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive is a grammatical case in Latin and German, marking ownership.

clue.text: Old Persian king with bone half bent back

indicators.note: half bent back means only the first half of the word is read backwards

parts.note: the radius is a bone of the forearm

explanation.surface: An ancient Persian monarch with a half-bent bone in his back.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of RADIUS, RAD, turns round to DAR, giving DAR plus IUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Darius the Great was an Achaemenid ruler of ancient Persia, an old Persian monarch.

clue.text: Contributes forcibly to argument — makes audible entrances

indicators.note: makes audible means the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: ways in are entrances

explanation.surface: Someone who forces their way into an argument and announces their arrival loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To weigh in is to join a debate forcefully with one's own opinion.
